summary.title: Let's Make a Voxel Engine
summary.one_liner: A tutorial series that walks through building a voxel engine in C++ on OpenGL, covering block rendering, chunks, landscape generation, collision, and later rendering techniques.
takeaways: Voxel engine concepts are introduced as an iterative series, starting with basic block rendering and building up to chunks and culling.
Core engine goals are efficiency (many voxels on screen), dynamic modification of any voxel, and an expansive world size.
Topics include chunk management, display lists vs vertex buffers, frustum culling, collision detection, and loading and saving.
Later articles cover advanced landscapes, voxel sprites, deferred rendering, SSAO, physics, particles, water, and scenery objects.
Rendering code uses the author's own wrapper around OpenGL, with OpenGL calls provided in some guides.
summary.summary: This Google Sites page is the home page for a series of voxel engine tutorials written by the author while building their own engine, which later became the game Vox. It lists the article sequence, from basic block rendering and data structures through chunks, landscape creation, culling, collision, and advanced topics like deferred rendering and SSAO. The guides assume familiarity with 3D graphics, 3D math, and a API such as OpenGL or Direct3D. Code is shown through a personal rendering wrapper over OpenGL, with raw OpenGL calls given in some places. The page also indexes articles on the author's Juice engine and general development topics.
